name: Metameric Fast-Flow Vascular Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Criteria for Metameric Fast-Flow Vascular Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of segmental or metameric distribution of vascular malformation with fast-flow characteristics
Imaging evidence (MRI, MRA, or angiography) demonstrating arteriovenous shunting and fast-flow vascular channels
Histopathological confirmation of abnormal arteriovenous connections if biopsy performed
Exclusion of other syndromic or isolated vascular malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation with metameric distribution plus imaging confirmation of fast-flow vascular malformation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities; biopsy is rarely required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental arteriovenous malformation with fast-flow shunting
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic metameric distribution involving skin, muscle, and bone

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulsatile vascular mass with bruit and thrill
pathognomonic.notes: Palpable thrill and audible bruit over lesion
searchTerms: pulsing vascular lump with sound and vibration
vascular mass with bruit and thrill

common.notes: Swelling often present in affected metameric segment

common.symptomName: Cutaneous erythema or discoloration over lesion
searchTerms: redness or color change over lesion

common.symptomName: Pain related to vascular engorgement or ischemia
searchTerms: pain from blood vessel swelling or poor blood flow
pain due to vessel blockage or pressure

common.notes: Increased local temperature due to high blood flow
searchTerms: heat over swollen or inflamed area

occasional.notes: Due to ischemia or venous hypertension
Secondary to ischemia or nerve compression
searchTerms: reduced muscle strength in arm or leg

occasional.notes: Due to chronic high-flow vascular changes

occasional.symptomName: Venous hypertension signs such as edema
searchTerms: signs of high venous pressure like swelling
leg swelling due to vein pressure
heart failure with high blood flow

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits from adjacent nerve compression
searchTerms: weakness or numbness due to nerve compression

rare.notes: Bleeding from fragile vessels within malformation

laboratory: Generally normal; anemia may be present if bleeding occurs
imaging: MRI/MRA showing fast-flow arteriovenous shunting in metameric distribution
Digital subtraction angiography demonstrating arteriovenous fistulas and nidus
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Physical exam revealing palpable thrill and audible bruit over lesion

distinguishingFeatures: Slow-flow vascular malformation without arteriovenous shunting
Absence of pulsatile mass or thrill
Triad of capillary malformation, venous malformation, and limb hypertrophy
Usually slow-flow lesions without high-flow arteriovenous shunting

redFlags: Neurological deficits indicating nerve compression or ischemia
references: Dubois J, et al. Vascular Malformations: Clinical and Imaging Aspects. Radiology. 2018.
International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies (ISSVA) Classification, 2018.
